findings.title: §6.3 overstates which output sections the Callback parser actually consumes
findings.problem: §6.3 says the new path must emit 'the headings the Callback parser (parseAgentAnalysis) depends on' and lists all six, including ## Notification Routing and ## Jira Tracking. Verified against investigation-callback/index.ts: parseAgentAnalysis only parses ## Summary, ## Key Findings, ## Answers to Your Questions, ## Recommended Actions (also ## Actions / ### 4.), and the no-impact keyword set. ## Notification Routing and ## Jira Tracking are output-contract sections emitted for humans/Jira, not parser inputs. Behavior is unaffected because the design reuses all six existing SKILL.md sections verbatim and requirements.md lists the same six.
findings.fix: Reword §6.3 to say the new path reuses the existing SKILL.md output-contract headings, of which only ## Summary, ## Key Findings, ## Answers to Your Questions, and ## Recommended Actions are parsed by parseAgentAnalysis, while ## Notification Routing and ## Jira Tracking are emitted for downstream consumers. No section-list change needed.

findings.title: §2 could note that interface HealthEvent omits rawEvent and declares sourceAccountId optional
findings.problem: Verified investigation-trigger/index.ts: interface HealthEvent has no rawEvent member and declares sourceAccountId optional. The normalizer must still emit rawEvent because it is part of the Health branch workflowInput key set and the AC-4 exact-key invariant. The design is internally consistent (it already states rawEvent is carried but not read), but an implementer could wrongly 'trim' rawEvent.
findings.fix: Add one clause to §2 stating interface HealthEvent declares sourceAccountId optional and has no rawEvent member, so emitting rawEvent satisfies the Router/workflowInput key set without being consumed by the Trigger, and must not be dropped.
